knowledge_point.title: Using the Scalar Function Multiple Rule for Differentiation

question.:question/problem: Find $(u(t)f(t))^{′}$ where $f(t)=[\begin{aligned}3 t - 3 \\ - 3 e^{t} \\ 3 t^{3}\end{aligned}]$ and $u(t)=t^{2}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the scalar function multiple rule, we can write

$$
(u(t)f(t))^{′}=u^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t)f^{′}(t).
$$

Let's find $u^{′}(t)$ and $f^{′}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{′}(t)&=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3 t - 3) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 3 e^{t}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3 t^{3})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ - 3 e^{t} \\ 9 t^{2}\end{aligned}]\\u^{′}(t)&=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t^{2})=2 t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(u(t)f(t))^{′}&=u^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t)f^{′}(t)\\&=(2 t)[\begin{aligned}3 t - 3 \\ - 3 e^{t} \\ 3 t^{3}\end{aligned}]+(t^{2})[\begin{aligned}3 \\ - 3 e^{t} \\ 9 t^{2}\end{aligned}]\\&=[\begin{aligned}2 t \left(3 t - 3\right) \\ - 6 t e^{t} \\ 6 t^{4}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 t^{2} \\ - 3 t^{2} e^{t} \\ 9 t^{4}\end{aligned}]\\&=[\begin{aligned}3 t \left(3 t - 2\right) \\ 3 t \left(- t - 2\right) e^{t} \\ 15 t^{4}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: [\begin{aligned}3 t^{2} - 6 t \\ 3 t^{2} e^{t} - 6 t e^{t} \\ - 3 t^{4}\end{aligned}]
[\begin{aligned}6 t \\ - 6 t e^{t} \\ 18 t^{3}\end{aligned}]
[\begin{aligned}9 t^{2} - 6 t \\ - 3 t^{2} e^{t} - 6 t e^{t} \\ 15 t^{4}\end{aligned}]
[\begin{aligned}3 t^{2} \\ - 3 t^{2} e^{t} \\ 9 t^{4}\end{aligned}]
[\begin{aligned}6 t^{2} - 6 t \\ - 6 t e^{t} \\ 6 t^{4}\end{aligned}]

question.:question/problem: Find $(u(t)f(t))^{′}$ where $f(t)=[\begin{aligned}- 3 t - 1 \\ 3 e^{t} \\ - 2 t^{3}\end{aligned}]$ and $u(t)=t^{2}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the scalar function multiple rule, we can write

$$
(u(t)f(t))^{′}=u^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t)f^{′}(t).
$$

Let's find $u^{′}(t)$ and $f^{′}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{′}(t)&=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 3 t - 1) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3 e^{t}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 2 t^{3})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3 e^{t} \\ - 6 t^{2}\end{aligned}]\\u^{′}(t)&=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t^{2})=2 t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(u(t)f(t))^{′}&=u^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t)f^{′}(t)\\&=(2 t)[\begin{aligned}- 3 t - 1 \\ 3 e^{t} \\ - 2 t^{3}\end{aligned}]+(t^{2})[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 3 e^{t} \\ - 6 t^{2}\end{aligned}]\\&=[\begin{aligned}2 t \left(- 3 t - 1\right) \\ 6 t e^{t} \\ - 4 t^{4}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}- 3 t^{2} \\ 3 t^{2} e^{t} \\ - 6 t^{4}\end{aligned}]\\&=[\begin{aligned}t \left(- 9 t - 2\right) \\ 3 t \left(t + 2\right) e^{t} \\ - 10 t^{4}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

[\begin{aligned}- 6 t \\ 6 t e^{t} \\ - 12 t^{3}\end{aligned}]
[\begin{aligned}- 6 t^{2} - 2 t \\ 6 t e^{t} \\ - 4 t^{4}\end{aligned}]

question.:question/problem: Find $(u(t)f(t))^{′}$ where $f(t)=[\begin{aligned}3 t^{3} - 3 \\ 1 - 3 t^{2} \\ 3 t - 2\end{aligned}]$ and $u(t)=e^{t}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the scalar function multiple rule, we can write

$$
(u(t)f(t))^{′}=u^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t)f^{′}(t).
$$

Let's find $u^{′}(t)$ and $f^{′}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{′}(t)&=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3 t^{3} - 3) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1 - 3 t^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3 t - 2)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}9 t^{2} \\ - 6 t \\ 3\end{aligned}]\\u^{′}(t)&=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(e^{t})=e^{t}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(u(t)f(t))^{′}&=u^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t)f^{′}(t)\\&=(e^{t})[\begin{aligned}3 t^{3} - 3 \\ 1 - 3 t^{2} \\ 3 t - 2\end{aligned}]+(e^{t})[\begin{aligned}9 t^{2} \\ - 6 t \\ 3\end{aligned}]\\&=[\begin{aligned}\left(3 t^{3} - 3\right) e^{t} \\ \left(1 - 3 t^{2}\right) e^{t} \\ \left(3 t - 2\right) e^{t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}9 t^{2} e^{t} \\ - 6 t e^{t} \\ 3 e^{t}\end{aligned}]\\&=[\begin{aligned}3 \left(t^{3} + 3 t^{2} - 1\right) e^{t} \\ \left(- 3 t^{2} - 6 t + 1\right) e^{t} \\ \left(3 t + 1\right) e^{t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: [\begin{aligned}3 t^{3} e^{t} - 9 t^{2} e^{t} - 3 e^{t} \\ - 3 t^{2} e^{t} + 6 t e^{t} + e^{t} \\ 3 t e^{t} - 5 e^{t}\end{aligned}]
[\begin{aligned}3 t^{3} e^{t} + 9 t^{2} - 3 e^{t} \\ - 3 t^{2} e^{t} - 6 t + e^{t} \\ 3 t e^{t} - 2 e^{t} + 3\end{aligned}]
[\begin{aligned}3 t^{3} e^{t} + 9 t^{2} e^{t} - 3 e^{t} \\ - 3 t^{2} e^{t} - 6 t e^{t} + e^{t} \\ 3 t e^{t} + e^{t}\end{aligned}]
[\begin{aligned}9 t^{2} e^{t} \\ - 6 t e^{t} \\ 3 e^{t}\end{aligned}]
[\begin{aligned}3 t^{3} e^{t} - 3 e^{t} \\ - 3 t^{2} e^{t} + e^{t} \\ 3 t e^{t} - 2 e^{t}\end{aligned}]

question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the scalar function multiple rule, we can write

$$
(u(t)f(t))^{′}=u^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t)f^{′}(t).
$$

Let's find $u^{′}(t)$ and $f^{′}(t).$

$$
\begin{aligned}f^{′}(t)&=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 3 t^{3} - 1) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3 t^{2} + 1) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 2 t - 2)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}- 9 t^{2} \\ 6 t \\ -2\end{aligned}]\\u^{′}(t)&=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(e^{t})=e^{t}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}(u(t)f(t))^{′}&=u^{′}(t)f(t)+u(t)f^{′}(t)\\&=(e^{t})[\begin{aligned}- 3 t^{3} - 1 \\ 3 t^{2} + 1 \\ - 2 t - 2\end{aligned}]+(e^{t})[\begin{aligned}- 9 t^{2} \\ 6 t \\ -2\end{aligned}]\\&=[\begin{aligned}\left(- 3 t^{3} - 1\right) e^{t} \\ \left(3 t^{2} + 1\right) e^{t} \\ \left(- 2 t - 2\right) e^{t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}- 9 t^{2} e^{t} \\ 6 t e^{t} \\ - 2 e^{t}\end{aligned}]\\&=[\begin{aligned}\left(- 3 t^{3} - 9 t^{2} - 1\right) e^{t} \\ \left(3 t^{2} + 6 t + 1\right) e^{t} \\ 2 \left(- t - 2\right) e^{t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
